name: Converge
label: Deathwish
lede: Jacob Bannon and Kurt Ballou started Converge in Salem, Massachusetts, as teenagers with a four-track. Thirty-five years on they run their own label and their own studio, draw their own covers, and still make the most carefully built noise in hardcore.

eras.title: Salem kids with a four-track
eras.text: Converge starts with teenagers in Salem covering hardcore and metal, then learning to write their own. By 1995 they have a second guitarist, a debut Bannon paid for himself, and Ballou's studio, which is still mostly a tape machine.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: A band name chosen because it wasn't a hardcore cliche
years.p: [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]] and [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] start out in Salem, Massachusetts, covering hardcore punk and heavy metal, with [[Jeff Feinburg|61a3233a-63dd-4ae2-ac08-68ac9994735b]] and [[Damon Bellorado|fd79eaf6-1179-4aa4-8fcd-b535a56cc94e]] soon in the line-up.
years.xp:
Bannon later told Decibel: "There are cooler, more evil, more descriptive band names out there, but I don't think anything else would really work for us."

The band recorded early demos on a four-track and began playing shows in mid-1991, per Wikipedia. Exclaim! also credits the Gravel demo, cut at West Sound Studio in Londonderry, New Hampshire, and put out on cassette.

years.h: [[Aaron Dalbec|5ea0f2e5-66d0-48ce-82d5-9c85d2fa4c39]] joins on second guitar
years.p: Dalbec, met through the Boston hardcore scene, turns Bannon, Ballou, Feinburg and Bellorado into a five-piece.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: Halo in a Haystack, paid for with nursing home wages
years.p: Bannon didn't like how the artwork turned out and decided he'd handle every piece of Converge art after this one.
years.xp:
Exclaim! says Bannon covered the pressing with money saved from his job at a nursing home. It came out on Earthmaker and Stolnacke; Exclaim! puts the release in spring 1994, Wikipedia gives August 10, 1994 and a vinyl pressing of 1,000 copies.

Hate5six has footage of the band from April 2, 1994, the earliest full set on that site.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: Different colleges, five hours apart, and a seven-inch with teeth
years.p: The 1995 seven-inch is a clear step up from Halo in a Haystack. Bannon later said of it, "It had teeth."
years.xp:
Members had gone to different colleges and the band came close to ending. Then the distance, about five hours between Montreal and Boston, turned out to be workable; Ballou says it "wasn't the end of the world."

Orionquest and Heliotrope released the record. The songs were collected on a 2003 compilation of the same name.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: Ballou names his studio GodCity, after a [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]] song
years.p: He starts recording other bands in 1995, and nearly every Converge album ends up made there.
years.xp:
Ballou told a Scion Music Conference audience in 2011: "When I first started the studio, my ultimate business goal was maybe someday I'll have my own phone line and I could have, on the answering machine, 'This is GodCity.'"

GodCity moved to its current Salem location in 2003.

eras.title: A bassist in the bushes
eras.text: Two bassists in a year, a festival set that wins over a label, and a producer from Today Is the Day. By April 1998 Converge is on Equal Vision and Nate Newton is the bassist who stays.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: Petitioning the Empty Sky is where Bannon first feels content
years.p: Ferret Records puts it out as a four-song seven-inch, then as a longer CD. The Saddest Day becomes a set staple.
years.xp:
Bannon told Noisey it was "one of the first times I felt really content in what I captured. It was hectic and unhinged." He called the guitar solo in The Saddest Day "almost a metal parody."

A radio session from the era shows what unhinged meant: "I hit myself with the mic stand in the head and I'm bleeding; I'm bleeding like a sieve." The band also covered Twisted Sister's Burn in Hell, which Bannon considered a heavy, well-made song that metal culture treated as a joke.

years.h: [[Stephen Brodsky|a0ff602c-7f3e-472d-8786-953da6cd7591]] of Cave In, still in high school, takes the bass
years.p: He replaces Feinburg. Ballou has to pull him out of class to record, and he hides in the bushes from the truant officer.

years.big: "Wow even the nerds/emo kids are kicking the shit out of each other."
years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: A headline slot in Northampton gets Converge a record deal
years.p: Steve Reddy of Equal Vision Records watches the Really Loud Music Festival set in April, then signs the band in July.
years.xp: The signing came out of that one festival set, per Exclaim!. Reddy says he was "totally impressed by them live." Equal Vision's first move was to reissue Petitioning the Empty Sky, out January 20, 1998 with three live radio tracks added.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: Steve Austin of Today Is the Day produces When Forever Comes Crashing
years.p: The first Equal Vision album is also Brodsky's only full-length with Converge.
years.xp: The band recorded at GodCity from December 22, 1997 to January 3, 1998, per Wikipedia. Equal Vision reissued it in 2005 with bonus tracks and new artwork by Aaron Turner of Isis.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: Nate Newton was headed for cabinetmaking and takes over bass instead
years.p: Newton joins part-time while still in Jesuit, which broke up in 1999, and stays for good.
years.xp: Newton told Aversion.com he had no job at the time and thought, "fuck it, I'll go." The alternative, he said, was spending the rest of his life as a cabinet maker.

eras.title: Down to four, up to Jane Doe
eras.text: Ben Koller arrives, Newton starts writing songs, Bannon turns Deathwish into a real label, and the band cuts Jane Doe in three studios. Aaron Dalbec leaves as it comes out, and the four who remain are the ones still touring.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: Ben Koller takes the drum stool, and his first show is at a Chinese restaurant
years.p: Bellorado left in early 1999 and John DiGiorgio filled in briefly. Koller, 19 and already a Converge fan, gets the job.
years.xp:
Koller told The A.V. Club in 2016: "I joined when I was 19 and fresh out of high school, so I was pretty intimidated by these seasoned older guys."

Ballou knew him from Force Fed Glass and Blue/Green Heart. Koller later formed [[Mutoid Man|d6c8e477-7221-47be-bab3-fe6980cf4284]] with Brodsky.

years.src: Wikipedia: Deathwish Inc. · Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: Bannon and Tre McCarthy make Deathwish Inc. a real label
years.p: A late-1999 decision to treat it as a business gets it going; the first release, in 2001, is a Converge split with Hellchild.
years.xp:
Bannon told Exclaim! in 2001: "We created a pro-band, proactive environment for bands to be treated as they would want to be treated." McCarthy had met the band at a Boston show, alongside Dalbec.

Wikipedia says the label now lists over 240 releases from 120-plus bands, and Converge has the most.

years.src: Wikipedia: Deathwish Inc.
years.h: Deathwish number one is a split with Hellchild
years.p: Deeper the Wound comes with a demo, a Depeche Mode cover and live tracks from Converge.

years.cap: Jane Doe, cover art by Jacob Bannon
years.src: Wikipedia: Jane Doe (album) · Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Louder: Converge's Jane Doe
yt: Concubine / Fault and Fracture, official video
years.h: Three studios later, Jane Doe
years.p: Recorded at Q Division, GodCity and Fort Apache, it is the first album with Newton and Koller and the last with Dalbec.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports the album cost about $11,000 and was recorded to six reels of two-inch tape. At Q Division, Newton recalls James Taylor, next door, sending his engineer over to complain about the noise. Bannon recorded vocals at Fort Apache, on the stage of a large room, in the dark and alone: "It was kind of apt for the material."

Early press was rough. Bannon told Exclaim! in 2012 that he keeps a giant binder and that 90 to 95 percent of it was hugely negative. Terrorizer still named it album of the year for 2001, and Decibel later ranked it first among the best metal albums of the 2000s.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Wikipedia: Jane Doe (album)
years.h: Newton's plan for Jane Doe is a hardcore record the kids would hate
years.p: Newton writes full songs for the first time, and Ballou has someone telling him he doesn't like what he's playing.
years.xp:
Newton told The A.V. Club in 2016: "I remember all of us wanting to write a hardcore record the kids were going to hate."

His first complete songs for Converge were The Broken Vow and Heaven in Her Arms, which moved the writing away from Ballou alone. Ballou has said Koller's arrival reinvigorated the band.

years.src: Louder: Converge's Jane Doe · Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Wikipedia: Jane Doe (album)
years.h: Bannon's Jane Doe cover has no Converge logo on it
years.p: Bannon made the cover himself with spray cans and ink, a downturned face and nothing else, and told Louder it "gave some order" to the chaos of the music.
years.xp:
Exclaim! adds that Equal Vision also disliked the kinetic, hard-to-read booklet. Reddy said later: "Not every band has a clear vision of what they want to do and Converge knew what they wanted."

In October 2021, French model Audrey Marnay said she was the basis for the cover image, taken from a May 2001 Marie Claire Italy photograph.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Louder: Converge's Jane Doe · Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: Dalbec plays his last show and Converge becomes four
years.p: Dalbec, busy with [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]], is gone after the Jane Doe release. Ballou's stance was that any other change would end the band.
years.xp:
Exclaim! says his last show was the album release around September 8. Wikipedia says he was asked to leave because of his commitment to Bane. Bannon told Louder the recording had already felt like a quartet: "we were not happy that our second guitarist just wasn't as present."

Newton remembers Ballou's rule for the four-piece: "If anything changes, it's over."

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: The week Jane Doe comes out, Ballou's engineering job disappears
years.p: Ballou is laid off as a biomedical engineer, and the severance lets him run Converge and GodCity full time.

eras.title: Two-by-fours and a switch to Epitaph
eras.text: Converge tours hard, gets hurt, leaves Equal Vision for Epitaph, and makes You Fail Me and No Heroes close to home in Salem.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: Security guards swing two-by-fours at Gainesvillefest
years.p: A fight at the Florida festival was filmed and spread online, with bass player Newton visible in the melee.
years.xp: Online guessing that Newton hit someone was wrong, per Exclaim!. Bannon recalled: "I looked over and see blood shooting everywhere and just a bunch of crazy stuff happening, and I just see Kurt just calmly packing his stuff up."

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: Converge signs with Epitaph, and Equal Vision's Steve Reddy is hurt
years.p: Equal Vision felt it was owed another album; Converge said the Petitioning the Empty Sky reissue had covered its contract.
years.xp:
Bannon told Noisey that Epitaph Records "had a lot of respect for our independence and our really unique character."

Reddy, by email: "I was hurt when they went to Epitaph because I thought we had really come through on every aspect of Jane Doe."

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: You Fail Me is the first Converge record to chart
years.p: Made at GodCity from March 2004, it reaches number 171 on the Billboard 200 and adds a glockenspiel and a piano from a studio neighbor.
years.xp:
Bannon titled it before writing anything, from a phrase he kept repeating in his journals. Newton said the "you" is meant to be "the royal 'you.'"

Newton called it the smoothest recording the band had done, since everyone lived close to the studio and could "pop in and pop out." Matthew Ellard mixed it in three days after repeated power outages. The band toured it with Cave In and Between the Buried and Me.

years.cap: Bannon at All Tomorrow's Parties, UK, 2004
years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: A guitar thrown over Ballou's shoulder finds Bannon's face in Leipzig
years.p: Six stitches, on the 2005 Aggressive Tendencies Tour with Terror, Cursed and Mare.
years.xp:
Newton's account: "Kurt got a little overzealous with his guitar and decided to throw it behind him, not realizing Jake was standing there." He heard a loud bonk, then saw Bannon on the stage with blood all over his face.

Everyone in the band, Newton says, has been to the hospital numerous times for this band.

years.cap: Converge at Eurockeennes, Belfort, France, June 2007
years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: No Heroes has nobody else in the control room
years.p: Ballou records, engineers and mixes the whole album at GodCity, the first Converge record with no outside producer. It reaches number 151 on Billboard.
years.xp: Ballou told Decibel the aim was to capture "the way we sound playing together." Bannon shifted his lyrics toward "we" and "our" and away from "I"; the band joked about calling the album The Rapist, which worried the label about retail placement.

eras.title: Dethklok's opening act
eras.text: Converge sells out bigger rooms, tours with the cartoon metal band Dethklok, and starts a numbered series of its own releases while the members multiply side projects: Old Man Gloom, Doomriders, Mutoid Man.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: Axe to Fall leaks two weeks early and still reaches number 74
years.p: Steve Von Till of [[Neurosis|a9416fb3-4d28-4575-abae-f0d160be83ed]] sings on Cruel Bloom, tweaking the lyrics and arrangement, and Ballou adds a choir.
years.xp: Three songs came from a Verge-In side project with Cave In members, including Effigy. Sean Martin, formerly of Hatebreed, recorded his part with a torn finger glued together with superglue. Ballou turned the record in at 11:30 p.m. on the last day.

years.src: Wikipedia: Converge (band) · Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: Converge opens for Dethklok and Mastodon on the Metalocalypse tour
years.p: Adult Swim's late-2009 tour, with High on Fire also on the bill, puts a hardcore band in front of a metal crowd.
years.xp: The Axe to Fall video debuted on MTV2's Headbangers Ball on November 7, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: Converge puts out its own seven-inch, CONCULT01
years.p: On My Shield, recorded at GodCity, is sold at European shows and online, with a laser-etched sun on the B-side.
years.xp: CONCULT02 followed in May 2011 as a split with Dropdead. Napalm Death's Shane Embury asked for CONCULT03 after hearing it; the 2012 split includes a Wolverine Blues cover with [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] and Tomas Lindberg.

years.cap: Bannon at Highfield Festival, Germany, August 2014
years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: A dog named Anna Belle gives All We Love We Leave Behind its title track
years.p: Bannon wrote it about missing her while on tour. The album peaks at number 70 on Billboard, four spots higher than Axe to Fall.
years.xp: Bannon called the song "an open letter to the things that I feel I've left behind" for the sake of the band. Ballou called the album "more like a collection of singles than anything we've done before." No Light Escapes was written in five minutes by Newton and Koller. Vinyl was delayed by a Beatles box set.

eras.title: Roadburn changes the plan
eras.text: A one-off Roadburn set with Chelsea Wolfe grows into an ensemble, then a full album. Jane Doe finally gets played live from start to finish.

years.src: Invisible Oranges: Blood Moon Rising · Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: At Roadburn, Converge plays Jane Doe start to finish, then brings Chelsea Wolfe on
years.p: For the album's 15th anniversary, the band plays it front to back in Tilburg, then returns with [[Chelsea Wolfe|60e8e938-365e-4429-a141-4c79eb49588d]], Ben Chisholm, Brodsky and Von Till for a slower set.
years.xp:
The Blood Moon show began with a Roadburn invitation. The band rehearsed for three days at GodCity Studio before flying to Europe, and Bannon said getting the ensemble to work live was "very challenging" since in the studio they have limitless tracks. Ballou was skeptical about the Jane Doe set: "We're not a sentimental band."

Jane Live came out on March 3, 2017.

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing
years.h: Twelve years on, Ballou remixes You Fail Me
years.p: You Fail Me Redux aims to sit more comfortably between Jane Doe and No Heroes. Alan Douches remastered it and Bannon repackaged it.
years.xp: Ballou's goal: "Retain everything that I thought was great about the original."

years.src: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing · Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: Five years and six kids later, The Dusk in Us
years.p: It follows the 2017 seven-inch I Can Tell You About Pain; 18 songs were recorded and 13 kept.
years.xp: Exclaim! says the four members had six kids in five years, and the record leans mid-paced and uneasy. Ballou told Decibel: "I don't think our lives getting more complicated makes our music any less emotional."

years.src: Knotfest: Bannon on Bloodmoon · Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: Bloodmoon: I takes five years and a pandemic
years.p: Made with Wolfe, Chisholm and Brodsky as equal partners, not guests, and finished remotely.
years.xp: Bannon told Knotfest the work started about five years before the interview, well before the pandemic, and that the idea of adding instrumentation went back to the late 1990s. They swapped demo ideas, then put it on ice between bursts of inspiration. "Everybody's writing lyrics; everybody's writing music; everybody's playing music."

eras.title: Back to four, twice
eras.text: After Bloodmoon, Converge go back to just the four of them and put out a short album and a second one within months.

years.src: Wikipedia: Love Is Not Enough
years.h: Back to just the four of them, in 31 minutes
years.p: Love Is Not Enough is the shortest Converge album, recorded at GodCity with all the guitar by Ballou; the first single, the title track, came on November 19, 2025.
years.xp:
Ballou told an interviewer the album goes back to regular Converge, "where we are much more comfortable in our roles." A second single, We Were Never the Same, followed on January 13, 2026.

Wikipedia lists Metacritic 84, with 5 out of 5 from Kerrang! and 7.4 from Pitchfork.

years.src: Wikipedia: Converge (band)
years.h: Hum of Hurt lands less than four months later
years.p: The twelfth album was announced on April 1 with a cryptic billboard in Boston teasing the date.

sources.title: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing, A Full History of Converge
